A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aquatic biota from lake sediments are a useful and robust proxy to reconstruct past climate.

, in order to obtain reliable quantitative reconstructions of climatic change from lake-sediments, it is important to use a variety of numerical techniques to assess the sensitivity and reliability (i.e. transferability) of the biological climate-proxy.

, in climate sensitive lake systems, the remains of aquatic biotia can be sensitive and trust worthy proxies, permitting quantitative reconstruction of past climatic condition with high temporal resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need for a greater focus on the statistical techniques used to assess climate-proxy data in palaeolimnological research, in order to improve the quality and robustness of climate-proxy data.
there is a need for more studies that use multiple statistical techniques to assess the reliability and utility of biological proxies from lake sediments.
the most appropriate statistical technique to use in a given case will depend on the nature of the data available, the questions being addressed, and the characteristics of the lake system.
